newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzanian inflation stable but trade deficit up.
newsitem.headline: Tanzanian inflation stable but trade deficit up.

text.p: Tanzanian inflation remained stable at 18.8 percent in October, unchanged from September, while the trade balance deteriorated, the Bank of Tanzania said in a monthly report available on Monday.
The inflation figure, based on the year-on-year rise in the Consumer Price Index, compares with 28.5 percent in the year to October 1995, it added.
The report said inflation was relatively high in the fuel, power, water and rental sectors.
Exports earned Tanzania $74.8 million in October, 27 percent up on $58.7 million in September and 26 percent on $59.4 million in October 1995, it added.
But the value of imports rose much faster, to $126.6 million in October 1996 from $119.0 million in September from $89.4 million in October 1995.
This left a trade deficit of $51.9 million, against $60.3 million in September and $30.1 million in October 1995, it said.
Except in the case of tea, for which the volume exported fell 23.4 percent, the volume of all traditional exports -- coffee, cotton, sisal, tobacco and cashew nuts -- increased.
Cumulative export earnings for the period January-October 1996 increased 14.3 percent to $583.6 million, against $510.6 million in the same period of last year.

The bank said it was not worried about the slight increase in the import bill. "The increasing trend points to an increasing confidence by the business community and to the government, given the redefined role of the private sector in the economy," it said.
Tanzania's overall food situation remained satisfactory for most staples during October except for wheat and maize.
The bank said the small deficit in maize could be offset by non-cereal foods such as bananas and cassava while imports could remedy the wheat shortage.

The government's revenue collection improved strongly during the July-October period reaching 180 billion shillings ($300 million) compared to an earlier estimate of 161 billion shillings. July-October receipts account for 32 percent of the year's estimate.
Tanzania's total external debt at the end of October was $7.87 billion.
